title: Nothing Good Happens Below the 200-Day Moving Average - Systematic Investor 341

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Nothing Good Happens Below the 200-Day Moving Average - Systematic Investor 341.docx

speakers: Alan Dunne (host, sitting in for Niels Kostrup Larsen)
Mark (co-host, finance academic and systematic investor)
summary: Q1 2025 Systematic Investor episode: Mark argues nothing good happens below the 200-day average, distinguishes measurable risk from uncountable policy uncertainty, and explains why uncertainty can create trends but shrinks signal-to-noise sized positions. Also discusses gold drivers, manager curiosity, and portable alpha as building blocks of cash/bonds plus risk premia.

coverage.note: intro; 200-day moving average as sentiment switch; US vs Europe divergence
rotation across markets; Q1 2025 CTA numbers; trend transition lag; tariffs and contract specs
contract delivery location matters (copper NY vs LME); recessions man-made; mortality table of expansions
postwar fewer policy errors; uncertainty vs risk distinction; uncertainty indices
VIX term structure inverted vs tariff uncertainty at highs; uncertainty reduces risky asset exposure; capex delays

intermediate trend speed as prior; searcher/adapter quants vs experts; uncertainty regimes
regimes and few historical analogues; quants over experts in unprecedented environments
Trump put and feedback loops; Fed reaction function uncertainty; QT slowdown

models rotate regardless of uncertainty (Jan 2025 Europe); curiosity topic anecdote (no separate claims)

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: nothing good happens below the 200 day moving average
claims.claim: When prices fall below the 200-day moving average, sentiment, selling pressure and volatility change, so the average acts as a regime switch for risk.
claims.conditions: psychology and media attention around the 200-day level
claims.testable: yes - simple moving average rule testable

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the US uh general stock market, you know, S SNP, NASDAQ, they're below the 200 day moving average
claims.claim: In March 2025 US indices were below their 200-day average while some sectors and European equities were well above, signalling rotation.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the sock gen CTA index is now down uh 25 basis points. The sockgen trend index down uh a little bit over 1% 1.07%
claims.claim: At end of March 2025, SG CTA was down 25 bp on the month and 2.23% for Q1, and SG Trend down 1.07% and just over 4% for Q1, driven by choppy equities, bonds and February commodity reversals.
claims.indicator: SG CTA and SG Trend index

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: it takes time for some of these revisions in trends to then actually be adjusted in the portfolio
claims.claim: Intermediate-term trend followers lag when trends change, causing underperformance in the transition; if new trends persist, CTAs later outperform long-only.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: it now matters what are the contract specs that you trade if you're in the commodities markets
claims.claim: Tariff gaps between New York and London delivery (e.g. gold, copper) make contract specification and delivery location matter for trend portfolio construction, not just liquidity.
claims.indicator: NY vs London metal price gaps (COMEX vs LME copper, gold)

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: most recessions are man-made because of bad policy decisions or bad choices by market participants and not from old age
claims.claim: Recessions are typically caused by policy mistakes or participant errors rather than age of expansion, and current uncertainty is policy-made.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: the economy has become more serviceoriented and you know historically some of the swings in the economic cycle were driven by you know um the inventory cycle
claims.claim: Cycles have lengthened because the economy is more service-oriented, so inventory-driven swings matter less.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: we might risk token ourselves into a recession
claims.claim: Uncertainty alone can talk the economy into a recession because firms postpone investment and consumers postpone spending.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: risk is what is countable which is measurable
claims.claim: Risk (countable volatility) differs from uncertainty (uncountable, policy-ambiguity), and volatility is backward-looking whereas uncertainty indices measure forward ambiguity.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: by looking at the count of stories and the amount of words about uncertainty about the words of policy changes that we can then use you know sort of like large databases from news
claims.claim: News-based uncertainty indices count stories on monetary, spending and trade policy and form a separate factor from volatility.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the VIX term structure, it's inverted. So we have high volatility in the front end and it's and then we have uh lower volatility longer
claims.claim: In late March 2025 the VIX curve was inverted while tariff and global policy uncertainty indices were at or near pandemic-level highs, showing that risk (volatility) and uncertainty are distinct.
claims.indicator: VIX term structure vs tariff and global policy uncertainty indices

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: there generally will be a view that you're going to reduce your exposure to risky assets
claims.claim: Higher uncertainty raises the required risk premium and causes investors to reduce risky assets, as in the US where uncertainty is greater than in Europe (where debt financing and ECB easing give more certainty).
claims.indicator: uncertainty indices vs risky asset demand
claims.testable: partly - uncertainty index regression on returns

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if I don't know what the tariff situation would be I don't know what tax policy will be. I don't know what monetary policy may be. Maybe I'll hold off my uh capital expenditures
claims.claim: Policy uncertainty causes firms to delay capex and consumers to delay big purchases, slowing real-economy decisions.
claims.indicator: policy uncertainty vs capex and sentiment

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: there's more likely to be sort of uh autocorrelation in the time series which means is that there's more likely to be trends
claims.claim: In high-uncertainty regimes hedgers and speculators adjust slowly (dollar-cost-average), producing autocorrelation and therefore trends.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: we're all signal to noise traders
claims.claim: Quant trend signals are discounted by noise, so when volatility or uncertainty rises the signal-to-noise ratio falls and positions shrink even if trends exist.
claims.indicator: return to risk ratio / signal-to-noise scaling

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the financialization of gold is that that creates easier for people to demand gold and push prices up
claims.claim: Gold's rise despite lower inflation reflects gold ETFs lowering transaction costs (financialisation, per Harvey research) and large central-bank buying, especially China, as demand for an asset governments cannot appropriate.
claims.indicator: gold ETF flows and central-bank purchases

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: intermediate trend following seems to work you know best
claims.claim: Across long data the intermediate trend speed works best, so use it as the Bayesian prior and tinker only a little around it.
claims.testable: yes - compare lookbacks over long data

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: a quant is more of a searcher and an adapter
claims.claim: Quants search large databases and adapt/optimise factors, while discretionary traders act as experts using uncountable information; with high uncertainty, systematic links may break.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: we can't really point to other periods in the past like this then we sort of say that you'd want to discount the quality of experts
claims.claim: If the environment is truly unprecedented, expert judgement has no past analogues and one should load up on quant traders who let price action speak.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: I'm going to do is look at what is actually happening into the price action
claims.claim: When policy-makers' words and deeds may diverge, following market price action is the second-best solution for trend followers and others.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: is there a Trump put and where is it
claims.claim: Whether a policy put exists matters: if stock prices keep falling, feedback loops into the real economy and monetary policy may eventually force a policy reversal, but the market was sceptical.
claims.indicator: policy put (government tolerance of falling stocks)

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if I don't know what the reaction function is then this is where we call uncertainty
claims.claim: Uncertainty can be defined as ignorance of the policy reaction function (Taylor rule); with sticky 3% inflation, a December cut, September 50 bp cut and QT slowing from $25bn to $5bn, the Fed's function was unclear.
claims.indicator: Fed reaction function, Taylor rule, inflation expectations above 3%

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: financial shocks are asymmetric
claims.claim: Negative shocks affect markets more than positive ones, so uncertainty is mostly a downside concern and investors move to safe assets, but that also cuts upside if uncertainty resolves well.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if you increase your exposure to trend following that's going to be a positive because one is is that because you're trading both assets from the long and short side
claims.claim: Raising trend exposure helps in high uncertainty because it is long/short with variable beta, diversified across currencies, commodities and non-US equities, and follows a disciplined rule to cut exposure when trends fall.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the overall the equity beta has come down and it's now more biased towards overseas equities
claims.claim: In Q1 2025 broker trackers showed CTA equity beta falling and rotating toward overseas equities, which is what the trend rule should do.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: when you have high uncertainty the committee will probably be biased or most people
claims.claim: Committees and individuals tend to take no action in high uncertainty, whereas a systematic model discounts trends by volatility and rotates (e.g. into European equities in January 2025) regardless of uncertainty.
claims.indicator: rotation from US to Europe in January 2025

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: they separate what they see from the facts versus what the bias is that they bring
claims.claim: A useful manager skill is observation: separating facts from the biases one brings; curiosity increases observation and helps find what others miss.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: strong conviction but loosely held
claims.claim: Good managers hold strong conviction but stay open to changing their mind with new facts, and creativity in seeing differently is needed because identical views give identical portfolios.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: first we look at a f price trends then we look at fundamental trends
claims.claim: A research rubric: price trends first, then fundamental trends, then regime, then valuation extremes and potential mistakes, then signal-to-noise (trend-to-noise ratio), while setting political names aside.
claims.indicator: price trend, fundamental trend, regime, valuation, signal to noise

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: only the paranoid survive
claims.claim: Ask one more why until answers are reasonable; trend followers stop at price because the link from fundamentals to price is unknown, and others go deeper to second-order effects.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: it's not the portable portion that's the problem. It's the alpha portion has been the problem
claims.claim: Portable alpha has come and gone because the alpha component often disappointed, not the portability; the trend is towards efficient capital use and factor rather than asset-class allocation.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: I could take my treasuries and then I could use that as collateral to put trend following on top
claims.claim: Portable alpha lets one hold Treasuries as collateral and add trend, momentum or other risk premia on top instead of a credit spread, mixing risk premia with core assets.
claims.indicator: portable alpha / return stacking with trend overlay
claims.conditions: cheaper products and better alpha offerings

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: when you combine anything with the S&P, it looks fantastic
claims.claim: Return-stacking results look strong partly because the S&P 500 has returned about 15% annualised for years, so durability is uncertain.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: when stocks are above the 200 day moving average and they continue to be above there
claims.claim: When equities stay above their 200-day average plain beta suffices and portable alpha on top drags; when assets fall below it, paying margin to stack alpha becomes more attractive as directional beta declines.
claims.indicator: 200-day moving average and portable alpha overlay
